title: Official blink(1) mk2 enclosure CAD reference
license_note: The exact LICENSE.txt at this commit states CC BY-SA 4.0; README.md still says 3.0. Preserve this discrepancy rather than silently substituting one. blink(1) is a ThingM trademark.
modifications: The assembly adjusts the diffuser to the level side rails of ThingM’s v3k metal frame and fits the parts locally at their joint. It adds a visual USB connector and a PCB based on the official MK2 v2c6 EAGLE layout. The board thickness follows the nominal two-layer design stack. Package heights are visual estimates. The API exposes shell, PCB-only and assembled variants. The preview page offers empty shell and PCB-only modes. The bundled STL files retain their original bytes.

alignment.status: The display model uses the front opening for length alignment and the straight metal side rails for height alignment.
alignment.common_axes: Frame convention: x width, y body length, z thickness. Model agent may apply one further rigid transform to the whole assembled object for Three.js Y-up.

aligned_diffuser_bbox.stage: After rigid alignment, before fitting the diffuser to the rail heights.

alignment.basis: The exports use different axes and have unequal lengths. The assembly aligns their width and thickness centers and their front min-Y planes. On the original frame at X=0, the straight side extends from about Y=2.715 to Y=16.992 with its edges at Z=0 and Z=6. These planes define the diffuser seats along both rails. The renderer seats the front and rear joints, then levels the joined frame and diffuser together. The adjustment retains the transverse curvature, engraved faces and rounded tail. See seating-fit.json for contact measurements.

topology_check.method: Triangles joined by vertex coordinates rounded to 4 decimal places.

alignment.usb_connector: Neither downloaded enclosure file includes a full USB-A metal connector. Any separately rendered connector is a visual reconstruction and must not be labeled official CAD.

usb_end_candidate.status: Geometric inference, not an official assembly instruction.
usb_end_candidate.basis: At Y=0.01, Z=3, central opening spans X=2.31..14.69 (12.38 units); at Y=10 and 19.9 it spans X=1.2..15.8 (14.6 units). The narrowed low-Y end is consistent with the USB-A connector neck.

renderer_orientation.coordinate_mapping: (x,y,z) in assembled frame coordinates -> (y-centerY, diffuserMaxZ-z, centerX-x), followed by uniform normalization
renderer_orientation.basis: Rigid orientation places the fixed blink(1) face upward and ThingM downward. Raw source meshes are unchanged.

geometry_units.interpretation: Likely millimetres, inferred from USB-A/device scale. STL does not encode units; these are model-coordinate dimensions, not certified production measurements.

physical_references.note: Official Hardware FAQ says mk2 has independently addressable LEDs on both top and bottom. Place luminous sources on opposing thickness faces, rather than splitting the top view into two flat panels.
Official variation page confirms dual RGB LEDs and metal + plastic design for mk2.
ThingM’s illuminated mk2 side photo shows straight upper and lower edges along the metal rail, a rounded tip and a diffuser that wraps around the back.
The USB-end view shows the straight metal side between the upper and lower plastic faces and the rounded front shoulders beside the plug.
ThingM’s exposed-board photo shows the two metal side rails flanking the PCB behind the USB plug.
The mk2 product photograph shows paired retention holes on the exposed USB plug and the molded diffuser wrapping the back of the metal rails.
X1 in the v2c6 board is the Molex 48037-1000. The manufacturer identifies a right-angle Type-A plug, with a recommended PCB thickness of 1.20 to 1.60 mm.
Appendix A, figure 6-9 provides the mating-face and contact dimensions used for the visual plug.
The manufacturer shows a bare mk2 PCB and its connector during adapter assembly. The v2c6 board file supplies the coordinates used here.

sources.evidence: Official text explicitly assigns LEDs 1 and 2 to top and bottom, respectively.
Actual page image inspected: A is top and B is bottom; the UI icons show upper/lower strips. No enclosure wordmarks label these icons.
Official renderer calls colors[0] topColor and colors[1] botColor. The corresponding top/bottom image assets have no readable wordmarks.

wordmark_correspondence.status: Confirmed on the local physical mk2 by device RGB readback and the user's optical identification, consistent with the existing project record. Manufacturer sources independently confirm top/bottom numbering.
wordmark_correspondence.note: Device readback establishes LED 1 red and LED 2 blue; the user directly identified blink(1) on the red face and ThingM on the blue face. The wordmark mapping is local physical evidence and project research, not a manufacturer quotation. Camera rotation never swaps these physical bindings.
reviewed_visuals: Official manual pages 4, 5 and 7, rendered with macOS PDFKit and visually inspected.
Official Blink1Control2 device-light-bg-top.png and device-light-bg-bottom.png, visually inspected; only diffuser contours are visible.
Official blink1 hardware/firmware_mk2/blink1mk2-reprogram-diag.jpg, visually inspected; power/ICSP annotations do not identify LED indices.
Getting Started / FAQ / faqss image alt, title and lazy source filenames; no index-to-wordmark annotation found.

visual_polish.source_geometry: The assembly uses the original engraved diffuser and metal frame meshes, with the rail alignment and joint fit described in alignment. At the USB shoulders, the renderer shades the outer walls of the metal and diffuser along the v3k corner radii. The shading follows the diffuser bevel and keeps the edges of the USB opening sharp.
visual_polish.supplemental_geometry: The visual USB plug uses a radiused folded shield with retention holes on both broad faces, a black insulating tongue and four staggered contacts. Its 11 mm exposed length is a display estimate. The 17.5 mm lip-to-X1 distance comes from the v2c6 EAGLE package outline. Rear solder tails meet the four X1 pads.
visual_polish.materials: The frame has a uniform satin metal finish. The USB plug uses its own fine directional grain. Both fixed light sources illuminate the frosted diffuser.
visual_polish.presentation: The catalog uses an orthographic orbit camera, bounded zoom, broad reflection cards and directional studio lighting.
visual_polish.scope: Illustration for design review; not engineering fit or optical calibration.
visual_polish.emission: The diffuser light field and both spill lights are centered over the opposed v2c6 LED packages. The two sources add in linear RGB before tone mapping.

usb_orientation.source: User physical observation in this design session
usb_orientation.blink1_side: +Y / open half of the USB connector
usb_orientation.contacts: Travel with the tongue and face the open half
usb_orientation.scope: Supplemental visualization geometry; no original CAD positions, wordmarks or LED identities changed.

seam_correction.cause: Dominant-axis UV projection switched inside a metal curve triangle, producing a tangent/anisotropy reflection discontinuity. Ray casting confirmed the bright pixels hit the opaque metal frame, not a plastic pillar.
seam_correction.correction: Continuous circumferential side-frame UVs; planar top/bottom UVs; per-triangle projection for other metal parts; matte finish and anisotropy disabled.
seam_correction.geometry: No bridge, cover strip or source CAD position change.

two_face_preview.display: Independent orthographic two-face schematic during loading, missing WebGL or context loss; also directly reviewable via ?view=faces.
two_face_preview.states: Resolved colors, #000000 off, and an unspecified target are distinct; reads the same presentation targets as the 3D model.
two_face_preview.scope: Code-native schematic, not a photograph or engineering drawing; original mascot and official CAD source bytes remain unchanged.
two_face_preview.wordmarks: Orthographic paths extracted from the fixed official diffuser STL engraving; no invented ThingM logo. These paths are CAD derivatives under CC-BY-SA-4.0. See inline source notes in studio.js and the preserved original enclosure license.

light_overlap.model: One continuous frosted diffuser, two fixed opposed light sources.
light_overlap.calculation: Smooth distance attenuation in model-local position; decode canonical sRGB source colors once and add their linear radiance before tone mapping. No average over source count and no hard face/UV split.
light_overlap.scope: Visual scattering parameters, not measured optics. Opaque metal, enclosure geometry, USB orientation and wordmarks are preserved.
light_overlap.data: Rendered mixture does not alter source RGB, Go playback plans or diagnostic 2D swatches.
light_overlap.verification: Production GLSL software checks cover additive radiance, source dominance, cross-face transmission, continuity, black clearing and pose-invariant identity; they do not certify physical optics.

seating_fit.scope: Display assembly in source CAD units. The frame extends slightly into the diffuser at the joint.
seating_fit.cause: The original diffuser seats diverge toward the rear. Fitting the long metal sides to those seats made the metal appear to grow taller behind the USB plug.
seating_fit.correction: Seat the frame against the diffuser at the front shoulders and rear tips, then level both parts together using the original metal planes as the height datum.
seating_fit.previous_fit: The 2026-11-15 frame fit addressed overlapping side surfaces and exposed USB-corner edges using side clearance, local shared-edge subdivision and front projection at the fitted height.

public_metadata_note: Published metadata retains manufacturer URLs, CAD attribution, model changes and LED mapping. Private project-note excerpts, local source paths, device identifiers and receipt paths are omitted; original handoff is retained privately.

pcb_layout.component_placement: Source EAGLE coordinates retained for the USB connector, controller, passives, testpoint, programming holes and both LEDs.
pcb_layout.revision_note: The user-provided v2c3 PDF is an earlier schematic. v2c5/v2c6 board files use WS2812B LED packages; the v2c6 board in the main hardware/schematic directory is the model reference. The separate dev/v2d layout is not used.
pcb_layout.appearance_reference: The public mk2 programming photo shows the white solder mask, a circular LED window and three plated programming holes. The v2c6 board file supplies the outline, hole and pad geometry and component placement. The photo does not identify its board revision.
pcb_layout.stackup_basis: v2c6 EAGLE layerSetup (1*16), 1.5011 mm dielectric and 0.0356 mm copper per side. The production board was not measured.
